lessons.title: Number Series Patterns
lessons.concept: Number series questions present a sequence of numbers following a rule. Common patterns include constant differences (arithmetic progression), constant ratios (geometric progression), increasing/decreasing differences, squares/cubes, or alternating operations. Identify the pattern by examining differences or ratios between consecutive terms.
lessons.formula: Check: difference (a2-a1, a3-a2...), ratio (a2/a1...), squares/cubes, or alternating patterns.
mistakes: Checking only the first two terms and assuming the pattern

lessons.title: Letter Series Patterns
lessons.concept: Letter series use alphabetical positions to form patterns. Convert letters to positions (A=1..Z=26) or observe shifts between consecutive letters. Patterns may involve constant shifts, increasing shifts, or alternating sequences.
lessons.formula: Map letters to positions; find step pattern (+1, +2, +3 or +2, +2, +2 etc.), apply to get next letter(s).
lessons.worked_example: Series: A, C, E, G, ? Positions 1,3,5,7 with step +2. Next is 9 -> I.
mistakes: Assuming a constant step when steps themselves change

lessons.title: Mixed and Alternating Series
lessons.concept: Some series alternate between two independent sub-series or combine different operations. To solve, split the series into odd-positioned and even-positioned terms and analyze each sub-series separately, or look for alternating operations (+, -, x).
lessons.formula: Try splitting: terms at positions 1,3,5 form one series; positions 2,4,6 form another. Or identify alternating operations.
lessons.worked_example: Series: 2, 3, 4, 6, 6, 9, ? Odd positions: 2,4,6,8? (+2). Even positions: 3,6,9 (+3). Next is 7th term (odd position) = 8.
mistakes: Trying to force a single pattern on an alternating series
Missing combined operation patterns (e.g., x2 then +1)
